title: BC Derivatization for Dissolved Marine Metabolites
author: Brittany Widner
materials: Prepare reagents. Unless otherwise stated plastic pipette tips are appropriate for all steps.

steps.title: Prepare primary stock mixes
steps.instruction: Make eight primary stock solutions (mix 1‑8) at 10 µg/mL (mix 1‑5, 7) or 20 µg/mL (mix 6, 8) in aged filtered seawater; label each as 10‑20 µg/mL as indicated. Mix 8 must be prepared fresh.

steps.title: Prepare secondary stock (100 ng/mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL of each 10 µg/mL mix (1‑5, 7) and 25 µL of each 20 µg/mL mix (6, 8) into seawater matrix and bring to a final volume of 5 mL to obtain a 100 ng/mL mixed‑metabolite stock.

steps.title: Prepare tertiary stock (5 ng/mL)
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of the 100 ng/mL secondary stock to seawater matrix and bring to a final volume of 5 mL to obtain a 5 ng/mL mixed‑metabolite stock.

steps.title: Prepare SIL‑IS solution (200 ng/mL)
steps.instruction: Make a 200 ng/mL ¹³C‑benzoyl‑chloride internal‑standard mix in aged filtered seawater. Derivatize this mix with ¹³C‑6‑benzoyl chloride using the same derivatization protocol as samples. Add 20 µL of this SIL‑IS to each sample to deliver 5 ng SIL‑IS per sample. For N = 55 samples, prepare at least 1.1 mL SIL‑IS solution; therefore derive >0.883 mL seawater (initial volume) because reagents add 24.5 % of the volume. Round up to 2 mL initial seawater (Vol i). After derivatization the total volume will be 2.490 mL (Vol t). Calculate required concentration of the spike solution: 622.5 ng total standard in 2 mL → 311.25 ng/mL. Use 62.3 µL of each 10 µg/mL primary mix and 31.1 µL of each 20 µg/mL primary mix (total 342.5 µL) and add 1 657.5 µL seawater matrix to reach 2 mL. Use the equations provided (Ns, Vol sp, Vol d, Vol i, 0.803 constant, etc.) for any other sample number.

steps.title: Prepare working reagent (5 % BC)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5 % v/v solution of benzoyl chloride in acetone. Use glass Hamilton syringes with metal needles (no plastic) for measuring acetone. Transfer benzoyl chloride with plastic pipette tips if needed. Make fresh daily. Work in a fume hood with PPE; benzoyl chloride is toxic, flammable, corrosive. Dispose of all BC waste as hazardous liquid/solid.

steps.title: Prepare 8 M NaOH solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve NaOH to 8 M; store indefinitely at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 0.01 M HCl solution
steps.instruction: Dilute HCl to 0.01 M; store indefinitely at room temperature in Teflon or glass containers.

steps.title: Derivatize samples and standards
steps.instruction:
For each 5 mL sample (or scaled volume):
1. Add 150 µL 8 M NaOH and invert 5 times.
2. Add 1 mL 5 % benzoyl‑chloride working reagent (glass or Teflon dispenser). Observe oily “beads”.
3. Mix for 5 min by vortex or manual inversion.
4. Add 75 µL phosphoric acid, invert 5 times; solution becomes clear (white precipitate may form later).
5. Add the calculated volume of SIL‑IS spike (e.g., 20 µL) as determined in the SIL‑IS preparation step.
6. Store derivatized samples at –20 °C if not processed immediately.

steps.title: Remove acetone (≥95 % by weight)
steps.instruction: Weigh each capped sample, record mass, then evaporate acetone using a Vacufuge (30 min) or a nitrogen stream (TurboVac, 30 °C, 7‑8 psi, 30 min). The required acetone removal equals the weight added by the working reagent plus any from the SIL‑IS addition.

steps.title: Separate precipitate
steps.instruction: For 5 mL samples centrifuge at 1000 × g, 22 °C for 15 min (low speed to avoid glass breakage). For 25 mL samples either centrifuge similarly or refrigerate overnight to let precipitate settle. Minimal plastic is used; avoid transferring precipitate when possible.

steps.title: Condition PPL SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Condition each Bond Elut PPL cartridge with 6 mL (one cartridge volume) Optima‑grade methanol. Keep cartridge wet; collect methanol waste in a glass tube for hazardous disposal.

steps.title: Rinse cartridge with HCl
steps.instruction: Rinse cartridge 4 times (4 cartridge volumes) with 0.01 M HCl. Do not let cartridge dry out. Collect HCl waste in the glass SPE manifold and neutralize with baking soda in a connected vacuum carboy.

steps.title: Load sample onto cartridge
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the entire supernatant (same volume as the original sample, e.g., 5 mL or 25 mL) to the cartridge using a glass Pasteur pipette. Minimize precipitate carry‑over but prioritize recovering all liquid. Allow liquid to drip by gravity or apply gentle pressure (<5 in Hg) for larger volumes.

steps.title: Final cartridge rinse and dry
steps.instruction: Rinse cartridge 4× with 0.01 M HCl, then pull air through at ~15 in Hg for 5 min to dry.

steps.title: Elute metabolites with methanol
steps.instruction: Slowly elute with 6 mL (one cartridge volume) Optima‑grade methanol into combusted test tubes at ~1 mL min⁻¹. If needed, apply a mild vacuum (<5 in Hg) to start flow.

steps.title: Transfer eluate to amber vials
steps.instruction: Transfer each eluate to an 8 mL combusted amber vial using a glass pipette. Label both caps and vials (e.g., with label tape). Store vials in a flammable‑free freezer or proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Dry samples in Vacufuge
steps.instruction: Place vials in an Eppendorf Vacufuge. Use the alcohol setting unattended for 3.5 h, then switch to the aqueous setting until completely dry. Periodically tap vials to break any white precipitate film that may inhibit drying. Over‑drying is preferred to residual moisture.

steps.title: Reconstitute and wash precipitate
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 5 % v/v acetonitrile/H₂O (Milli‑Q) to each vial, vortex thoroughly (precipitate largely remains insoluble). Centrifuge at 1000 × g, 22 °C for 15 min. Transfer the clear supernatant to a 2 mL centrifuge tube (for 5 mL samples skip to step 12.7/12.8; for 25 mL samples continue to step 12.4). Dry the transferred liquid on the Vacufuge aqueous setting at 30 °C until dry. Store dried material at –20 °C until LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Add injection standards
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL 5 % v/v acetonitrile/H₂O containing 50‑300 ng/mL deuterated injection mix (typical RP method). Vortex, then transfer to centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 000 × g, 22 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Transfer to LC‑vial insert
steps.instruction: Transfer a defined volume (e.g., 80 µL) of the supernatant to an LC‑vial insert, vortex briefly.

steps.title: Add final acetonitrile
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL acetonitrile to the LC vial (with insert) to aid injection.

steps.title: Prepare d5‑SIL‑IS (optional)
steps.instruction: Make a 1000 ng/mL d⁵‑benzoyl‑chloride SIL‑IS mix in aged filtered seawater. Derivatize as above and add 50 µL to each sample to deliver 25 ng d⁵‑SIL‑IS. Follow steps 2.2‑2.3 for calculations.

steps.title: Clean cartridge edges
steps.instruction: Using a Kimtech wipe, remove any HCl droplets from cartridge edges and manifold needle tips before elution to avoid excess HCl in final eluate.

steps.title: Complete methanol elution
steps.instruction: After visible methanol has been collected, apply a vacuum of 5‑10 in Hg to pull any remaining methanol from the cartridge into the elution vial.

steps.title: Create pooled QC sample (optional)
steps.instruction: Combine equal volumes (e.g., 10 µL) from each sample into a single LC‑vial with insert to generate a pooled QC. Use a fresh pipette tip for each transfer. Calculate required pool volume based on number of samples and desired injection volume (e.g., 5‑10 µL per sample for 50 samples yields ≥50 µL pool for positive mode, ~100 µL for both ionization modes).

steps.title: Store final extracts
steps.instruction: Store all prepared LC‑vial inserts at 4 °C (above freezing) to minimize precipitation until LC‑MS analysis.
